Its phosphate anion is hard to oxidize, and it is thermodynamically tolerant of the sulfide electrolyte, so it should give a small interfacial penalty at 4.0 V.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (well above 2 eV), electronically insulating lithium-rich phosphate. It is a well-known cathode coating for LiCoO2 and is chemically compatible with both Li6PS5Cl and LiCoO2. Its phosphate anion is hard to oxidize, and it is thermodynamically tolerant of the sulfide electrolyte, so it should give a small interfacial penalty at 4.0 V.

LiF is a very wide-gap, electronically insulating Li-rich halide. Fluoride is the most oxidation-resistant halide, so it should stay stable against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V. Li-F is also a very strong, low-reactivity bond, so LiF should be less prone than the phosphate to reducing the sulfide electrolyte (Li6PS5Cl) or releasing S/P oxidation products. This should give a lower contact penalty than the Li3PO4 baseline (penalty 0.337 eV, bin 16).
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 baseline gave a contact penalty of 0.337 eV/non-Li atom, driven by reaction with the sulfide electrolyte to form P2O5, SCl4 and SO2. This points to a need for a coating with lower sulfide reactivity and high oxidative stability, which a fluoride is expected to provide.

Both earlier phosphate and fluoride coatings reacted with Li6PS5Cl, so an oxide with a high-valence, reduction-resistant cation is a different chemical route to a lower contact penalty.
